sections.h2: How does selling a house in Kenosha work?
sections.html:
A Kenosha homeowner can list with an agent, sell without one, or accept a cash offer from a buyer who takes the house as it stands. The Census Bureau estimates 99,239 residents in the city as of July 1, 2025, and the 2020 census ranked it fourth among Wisconsin cities.

Each route ends the same way at the Kenosha County Register of Deeds: a deed, an electronic transfer return and a fee. What changes is the timeline and who pays for repairs. A listing means showings, an inspection and a lender's appraisal. A direct cash sale usually removes the lender step, so closing can follow the title work instead of a loan approval.

sections.h2: What kind of city is Kenosha for a home seller?
sections.html:
Kenosha sits on Lake Michigan in southeastern Wisconsin, about 32 miles south of Milwaukee and 49 miles north of Chicago, with the Metra Union Pacific North line ending at its station. It was settled in 1835 as Pike Creek, renamed Southport in 1837, and took the Kenosha name when it became a city in 1850.

For most of the 20th century the city built cars. Rambler, Nash, Hudson and American Motors vehicles came off Kenosha lines until 1988, and the former AMC lakefront plant site became HarborPark, now lakeside condominiums, a marina and the Kenosha Public Museum. Today Snap-on and Jockey International have their headquarters here, and outlying business parks hold warehouses and distribution centers.

Locals describe three areas:

  • Downtown and HarborPark: the lakefront, with Allendale directly to the south.
  • Uptown: a mixed residential and small-business area that includes Brass, Lincoln Park and Wilson Heights.
  • West of the I: the part of the city beyond Interstate 94, which residents often call "the county."

Buyer interest differs by area, so a seller in Wilson Heights and one in HarborPark should expect different comparable sales and different buyer pools.

sections.h2: Why do commuting, schools and winters matter to Kenosha buyers?
sections.html:
They set who shops for your house and what they look for. Nearly half of the city's workforce commutes outside Kenosha County, and a 2016 study found many of those workers hold jobs in healthcare, manufacturing and professional services. Lower housing costs than the Chicago area draw them, so a house close to I-94 or the Metra station tends to appeal to that group.

Families look at Kenosha Unified School District, which runs 23 public elementary schools, five middle schools, seven charter schools and six high schools, among them Bradford, Tremper, Indian Trail and Reuther Central. Students also live near the University of Wisconsin-Parkside, Carthage College and the Gateway Technical College campus.

Weather shapes inspections. NOAA normals show about 37.6 inches of precipitation and 36.2 inches of snow in a typical year, the record low is minus 31 degrees Fahrenheit, and the city has had blizzards that dropped 19 and 23 inches. Buyers' inspectors in a climate like that spend time on roofs, gutters, basements and furnaces, so those are the items most likely to appear in a repair request. A cash buyer prices them in and skips the negotiation.

sections.h2: What are the steps and costs when a Kenosha house changes hands?
sections.html:
Wisconsin charges the seller, not the buyer, a transfer fee of 30 cents for each $100 of value or fraction thereof (Wis. Stat. 77.22). On a $225,000 sale that works out to $675. The Kenosha County Register of Deeds collects it when the deed is recorded, and the county keeps 20 percent while the balance goes to the state.

The steps run in this order:

  • Sign the purchase contract and open title work.
  • Complete the electronic Real Estate Transfer Return on the Wisconsin Department of Revenue site. The county requires the eRETR receipt for every conveyance that is not exempt.
  • Record the deed at the Register of Deeds, 1010 56th Street, Kenosha. Real estate documents are recorded Monday through Friday from 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. A satellite office operates at 19600 75th Street in Bristol.
  • Pay off any mortgage, lien or unpaid tax from the proceeds.

Transfers by will, descent or survivorship are exempt from the fee under Wis. Stat. 77.25, as are transfers from a parent to a child for nominal consideration. An heir who later sells an inherited Kenosha house still pays the fee on that sale, because the sale itself is not exempt.

sections.h2: Do Kenosha sellers have to give the buyer a condition report?
sections.html:
Usually yes. Chapter 709 of the Wisconsin Statutes requires an owner who sells a property with one to four dwelling units to give the buyer a completed Real Estate Condition Report within 10 days after the contract is accepted. A buyer who does not receive it may rescind within two business days after those 10 days end and get the deposit back (Wis. Stat. 709.02).

Personal representatives, trustees, conservators and court-appointed fiduciaries who have never lived in the house are excused from the report, which matters for estates. Transfers that are exempt from the transfer fee are also exempt from the report. Ask the closing attorney or title company whether your sale falls under an exemption.

sections.h2: How are Kenosha property taxes handled at closing?
sections.html:
The tax bill for the year is divided between you and the buyer at closing, and any unpaid balance is paid from your proceeds. Wisconsin lets owners pay real estate tax in two equal installments, due January 31 and July 31, and a bill under $100 is due in full by January 31 (Wis. Stat. 74.11). If a first installment is not received within five working days after January 31, the entire unpaid balance becomes delinquent, and interest and penalties run from the preceding February 1.

The next first-installment date is January 31, 2027. Ask the Kenosha County Treasurer or the city treasurer for the paid-to date and the amount still owed before you sign.

faqs.q: How much does it cost to sell a house in Kenosha, Wisconsin?
faqs.a: The fixed state charge is the transfer fee of 30 cents per $100 of value, which is $600 on a $200,000 sale. A listing adds agent compensation, repairs and carrying costs, while a direct sale to a cash buyer removes most of those lines. Ask your title company for a net sheet so the numbers are on paper before you choose.

faqs.q: Who collects the real estate transfer fee in Kenosha?
faqs.a: The Kenosha County Register of Deeds collects it when the deed is recorded. You complete the electronic transfer return with the Wisconsin Department of Revenue first, and the county requires the receipt for every conveyance that is not exempt.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Kenosha house that needs repairs?
faqs.a: Yes. Repairs are your choice, and a seller covered by chapter 709 must report defects the owner is aware of on the condition report. Some buyers will take the house as is and price the work, which spares you contractors and inspection requests.

faqs.q: Is an inherited Kenosha house taxed when I sell it?
faqs.a: The transfer itself by will or descent carries no Wisconsin transfer fee, so the heir does not owe it for inheriting. The later sale to a buyer is a new conveyance with the 30 cent fee. Ask a tax professional about income tax on any gain.

faqs.q: When are Kenosha property taxes due?
faqs.a: Wisconsin real estate tax is due in two installments, January 31 and July 31, unless the bill is under $100 or the municipality has adopted a multi-installment ordinance. A late payment can make the full remaining balance delinquent, so settle it before listing.
